# ADR-0005: Geometry demo corridor connects to the live main world

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-07

## Context

The original Phase 4 geometry demo created a self-contained destination world. The player could traverse the four-dimensional corridor correctly, but the exit landed in a separate slice with no connection to Somnium's existing populated main world. That made the exit appear empty and duplicated terrain ownership.

## Decision

The demo corridor will terminate in the existing `somnium-main` slice at a configured exit anchor sampled from the live main-world terrain. The anomaly is registered as an explicit graph node between the demonstration room chunk and the main-world chunk that contains that anchor.

The application's one main-world `WorldManager` owns and streams main-world chunks. It shares the demo's `SpatialChunkGraph` and `BabylonGeometryAdapter`, and is borrowed by the demo for preview rendering and destination chunk streaming. The demo does not create, duplicate, or dispose a second destination manager.

A cross-slice adjacency exists only because the traversable corridor is explicitly registered. The main-world destination chunk remains a logical neighbour before load, and becomes a resident neighbour when the real manager registers it. On unload, the resident reference is removed without deleting the corridor topology.

## Consequences

- Traversal arrives on actual main-world terrain rather than an isolated generated destination.
- The same main-world chunk manager owns the chunk before, during, and after anomaly traversal.
- Portal preview and player destination use the same streamed chunk meshes.
- Chunk graph adjacency can be inspected and tested independently of Babylon rendering.
- The geometry demo currently retains its own player/camera update loop after arriving in the main-world slice. Full gameplay-mode and simulation-system handoff is intentionally a later application-layer change.

docs/decisions/ADR-0006-free-camera-and-corridor-preview.md
_______
# ADR-0006: Independent 4D Inspection Camera and Continuous Corridor Preview

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

The geometry demo's third-person camera follows the player and does not provide an independent way to inspect the anomaly. During corridor traversal, the destination preview was positioned very close to the exit and the corridor shell was highly opaque, making the connected world difficult to see from inside the tunnel.

## Decision

Keep player-follow mode as the default and add a separate free inspection mode controlled by `C` or the demo HUD. The free camera owns its own position, orientation, active slice, input state, and optional corridor transit state. It does not mutate the player's position or traversal state. Character input is suppressed while free inspection is active and restored when follow mode resumes.

Outside a corridor, free-camera movement uses three render-space controls: forward/back, strafe, and vertical movement. During corridor inspection, the controls map to the transported four-dimensional frame: the corridor tangent plus its three perpendicular directions. The 4D position is retained in ambient coordinates; the Babylon camera receives the current 3D display mapping.

Keep a destination aperture ahead of the active viewer in both directions. The third-person camera aims at the aperture, and free-camera transit takes precedence over a stationary player transit when selecting preview progress. Use a lower forward-looking destination preview camera, enlarge the aperture to fill more of the corridor, and keep the corridor shell translucent (default opacity 0.22) with depth writing disabled. Keep the aperture a bounded distance ahead of the current viewer, with look-ahead scaled from measured corridor arc length and clamped to 8–22% of the route, so it remains visible early in both forward and reverse transit.

## Consequences

- Camera inspection no longer requires moving the player.
- A user can enter free inspection while the player is already in transit; the camera is initialized from the current transit state but remains independently controlled.
- A free camera can independently enter and exit the same corridor topology and change render slice without moving the player.
- `C` always toggles modes while the geometry demo is active; the button provides the same action.
- The destination window remains a bounded distance in front of the active viewer as the viewer advances or retreats, including independent free-camera transit.
- The camera's 4D state remains authoritative for navigation; its 3D display is necessarily a projection.
- A translucent corridor shell improves visibility but may require additional GPU-specific transparency tuning once browser rendering is profiled.

## Alternatives considered

### Reuse the player traversal controller for camera movement

Rejected because moving the camera would then move the character, preventing independent inspection and coupling view control to gameplay state.

### Move the portal to a fixed point just before the destination

Rejected because the aperture becomes too small in perspective and can fall behind the camera near the exit. The preview now stays a bounded distance ahead of the current progress.

### Remove the corridor shell

Rejected for this step because the tunnel is useful for understanding the anomaly's shape. A translucent shell preserves the visual cue while reducing occlusion.

docs/decisions/ADR-0007-hypercube-chamber-and-corridor-network.md
_______
# ADR-0007: Hypercube Chamber and Multi-Corridor Demo Network

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

The Geometry Demo previously started in the Poincare test chamber and represented one active corridor at a time. A 4D geometry test chamber needs its own world slice, its own test geometry, and a connection to the existing Poincare chamber. The Poincare chamber must remain connected to the live main world.

## Decision

Create a Euclidean slice `geometry-demo-4d-chamber` at `w = 140`. Render a tesseract consisting of 16 vertices and 32 edges. Rotate its 4D vertices in the XW plane and project them to the chamber's 3D view. Keep the tesseract's mathematical topology and projection independent of Babylon.js; the demo renderer owns only its derived line mesh and material.

Register a second traversable, bidirectional `SpatialCorridor` with its own `CorridorChunk`. The demo graph now contains the route:

`4D Hypercube Chamber -> 4D Corridor Chunk -> Poincare Chamber -> Main-World Corridor Chunk -> Somnium Main World`.

Compose the existing single-corridor traversal controllers using `CorridorTraversalNetwork`. The network selects traversal routes from explicit topology neighbours and synchronizes the active slice across controllers. It does not infer adjacency from fourth-coordinate distance.

The Geometry Demo menu option starts in the 4D chamber with the independent free camera. `E/Q` changes the viewer's W coordinate within the chamber's explicit bounds; `W/S`, `A/D`, and `R/F` control the three ordinary spatial view directions. In a corridor, the same input groups resolve to tangent progress and the three transported cross-section axes.

## Consequences

- The original Poincare chamber remains intact and now acts as an intermediate node with two anomaly routes.
- The original route into the actual main world is retained.
- Each anomaly remains an explicit, independently addressable corridor chunk.
- Multiple corridor controllers can coexist while only a route adjacent to the current slice can begin player traversal.
- The tesseract math is reusable outside Babylon.js and can later feed a GPU renderer.
- Browser-specific visualization is confined to the renderer adapter.

## Limitations

- This is a projected wireframe tesseract, not volumetric 4D rasterization.
- Free-camera W movement changes the viewer coordinate used for the 4D projection; it does not add free W motion to ordinary 3D player physics.
- Live browser/WebGL verification remains pending.

docs/decisions/ADR-0008-corridor-proper-length-and-hypercube-visibility.md
_______
# ADR-0008: Intrinsic corridor length and visible tesseract rendering

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

The demo corridors crossed large ambient fourth-coordinate and terrain-elevation differences. Traversal distance was calculated directly from the ambient R4 arc length, making short demonstrations take a long time. The tesseract renderer used a one-pixel LineSystem while the follow camera targeted the player, which made the object difficult to notice at the default viewpoint.

## Decisions

1. Add `intrinsicLengthScale` to `SpatialCorridor`, defaulting to `1`. Its allowed range is `(0, 1]`. Proper distance is ambient sampled arc length multiplied by this value. This represents metric compression within an anomaly without altering the world slices, ambient centreline, corridor chunks, or topology.
2. Set both geometry-demo anomalies to `0.32`, and configure demo traversal to 12 units/s walk, 18 units/s sprint, and 10 units/s for entities.
3. Render the tesseract as one dynamically updated tube mesh for its 32 edges plus 16 visible vertex markers. Retain engine-independent R4 projection and XW rotation.
4. Render the tesseract as visible chamber geometry, but keep the follow camera centered on the character model. During corridor traversal, the explicit render-anchor target takes precedence. The earlier tesseract-focused camera behavior was superseded by ADR-0010.

## Consequences

- Existing corridor definitions remain compatible because the new property defaults to `1`.
- Distant slices remain distant and explicitly connected; topology does not change.
- Demo travel time is reduced without changing the destination's 4D coordinate.
- The tesseract uses 17 render meshes (one edge mesh and sixteen small markers) sharing one material. This is a modest, bounded cost for the isolated test chamber.
- Camera focus remains player-centric; the tesseract is inspected by moving or orbiting the camera, not by displacing the character-follow target.
- The browser still needs a manual WebGL pass to confirm visual appearance on the target GPU/browser.

docs/decisions/ADR-0009-true-hypercube-cross-sections.md
_______
# ADR-0009: Render the tesseract as true 3D hyperplane sections

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-08

## Context

The previous chamber renderer projected nominal 4D vertices into 3D with a W-dependent perspective scale. This did not show the 3D slice encountered by a camera at a particular W coordinate. A separate vertex-generation defect also caused all sixteen generated corners to coincide because the `Array.from()` callback's element parameter was mistakenly used as its index.

## Decision

Represent the chamber view as the intersection of a rotating tesseract with the camera's current 3D hyperplane `W = viewerW`.

Apply a compound rotation in the XW, YW, and ZW planes. Intersect each original cubical 3D facet with the W hyperplane, construct planar polygons from their edge intersections, deduplicate vertices and edges, and render the resulting closed polyhedral boundary.

Keep the mathematical slicing engine-independent. Babylon is responsible only for the translucent surface mesh, tube edges, vertex markers, and reusable dynamic buffers.

## Consequences

- Moving in ordinary X/Y/Z space changes the camera's viewpoint on the same 3D section.
- Moving along W changes the section geometry itself, including its number of vertices and faces.
- The central section can be an oblique polyhedron rather than a constant cuboid.
- A slice outside the rotated tesseract is empty by definition.
- The old perspective-only projection helper is removed from the active tesseract path.
- The renderer has bounded reusable capacities (32 section vertices and 64 section edges), far above the known section complexity of a tesseract.
- A live browser/WebGL visual pass is still required after automated tests.

## Verification invariants

- 16 unique four-dimensional tesseract vertices and 32 original edges.
- Axis-aligned central section: 8 vertices, 6 quadrilateral faces, 12 edges.
- Default oblique central section: 12 vertices, 8 faces, 18 edges.
- Every edge of a closed section is incident to exactly two faces.
- W movement and 4D rotation change the generated section geometry.

docs/decisions/ADR-0010-render-space-third-person-camera.md
_______
# ADR-0010: Render-Space Third-Person Camera and Unrestricted Orbit

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

The shared third-person follow camera previously constructed its boom in authoritative world coordinates and projected the resulting point. In compactified Poincare slices, a fixed world-space offset can become extremely small in render space. The same camera controller is reused after anomaly handoffs, so the apparent camera distance changed substantially when the active slice transform changed. The geometry-demo camera also had a special focus override aimed at the tesseract rather than the character model.

The movement controllers use `R` as a vertical axis in some modes and called `preventDefault()` for every `R` keydown. That intercepted browser reload shortcuts such as Ctrl+R and Cmd+R.

## Decisions

1. Express third-person camera distance in render-space units. Project the character root first, then construct the camera boom around the rendered character focus. This keeps camera framing consistent when the active world slice changes its spatial transform.
2. Derive the character focus from the projected root plus a scaled model-height offset. Do not special-case the tesseract as the follow target. Explicit corridor render-anchor positions and targets remain authoritative while traversing legacy Bezier corridors.
3. Add right-mouse-drag orbit control to the follow camera. The orbit pitch is continuous and is not clamped to an arbitrary gameplay angle. A pitch-dependent camera up-vector transports orientation continuously across the poles. The existing left-drag character turning remains unchanged.
4. Preserve wheel zoom, lower the minimum boom distance, and substantially increase the maximum zoom distance. The main-world and geometry-demo camera presets may use different defaults and limits.
5. Ignore movement keydowns while Ctrl, Meta, or Alt is held. Normal `R` movement remains available, while browser/system shortcuts are allowed to propagate.

## Consequences

- The same render-space camera distance is maintained in Euclidean and Poincare slices, including after a slice transition.
- Camera zoom is no longer inadvertently compressed by the world projection.
- The 4D preview room's default follow view centers on the character model; the tesseract remains visible as chamber geometry.
- Right-drag can orbit through vertical orientations without a fixed pitch clamp. Left-drag continues to turn the character.
- Ctrl+R and Cmd+R are no longer suppressed by movement handlers.
- Camera placement is clamped through the active transform's render-chart constraint when one is available, preserving the open-ball validity requirement of Poincare charts.

docs/decisions/ADR-0011-optical-metric-and-cpu-reference-rays.md
_______
# ADR-0011: Optical Metric and CPU Reference Ray Solver

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

Somnium's geometry system now has authoritative 4D ambient positions, independent 3D world slices, multiple intrinsic slice geometries, and continuous anomaly influence fields. The next step is light propagation through those environments. Reusing the player's movement freedom or Babylon's rendering projection would couple unrelated systems and would make optical path lengths incorrect in curved charts.

## Decisions

1. Optical configuration is independent of player traversal. Anomaly optical permissions default to disabled and have independent directionality, W coupling, W reach, refractive index, transmission, and attenuation values.
2. Optical W coupling reuses the resolved anomaly center, inner radius, outer horizon, and shared smootherstep function. It does not use player freedom/reach multipliers or character statistics.
3. Optical ray positions and canonical momenta are represented in authoritative ambient R4. W is a spatial dimension; the ray's integration parameter and accumulated travel time are separate quantities.
4. A 3D slice optical metric is `n^2 * g_slice`. It is lifted into ambient R4 using the slice's orthonormal tangent frame and normal direction.
5. The ambient cometric is evaluated directly. At exactly zero W coupling, the normal direction is constrained and the cometric remains finite and positive-semidefinite; the implementation does not place infinity in a matrix.
6. The CPU reference solver integrates Hamilton's equations with adaptive RK4 step-doubling and records deterministic diagnostics. It is independent of Babylon.js.
7. Invalid geometry/chart samples are rejected by the metric provider and propagate through the solver. The solver does not silently clamp or swallow Poincare domain errors.
8. Phase 16A does not alter renderer, lighting, movement, camera, chunk streaming, or optical topology traversal. Those are later milestones.

## Consequences

- Euclidean and curved slice metrics can share one ray-state/integration API.
- The Poincare metric can be sampled through `SpatialTransform.metricAtWorld()` without involving render coordinates.
- Anomaly W optical coupling can be tuned independently of player W movement.
- A finite cometric can represent a zero-W constrained region without a singular stored tensor.
- The CPU solver provides a deterministic baseline for later scene intersections, cross-slice transport, debugging, and GPU implementations.
- The reference solver uses finite-difference derivatives and is not yet suitable as a high-ray-count real-time renderer.

docs/decisions/ADR-0012-slice-native-optical-intersections.md
_______
# ADR-0012: Slice-Native Optical Geometry and Intersections

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-08

## Context

Phase 16A introduced an engine-independent ambient R4 optical metric and CPU Hamiltonian ray integrator. Rays now need to interact with the world's actual surfaces without confusing authoritative geometry with Babylon's projected render meshes.

## Decisions

1. A scene-scoped `OpticalSceneRegistry` owns copied, authoritative slice-local triangle geometry and analytic terrain registrations.
2. Every registered surface has a stable object ID, `sliceId`, optional 3D chunk address, material contract, enabled state, and revision. Queries are slice-isolated and can additionally filter to explicit resident chunk addresses.
3. Triangle registrations own deterministic median-split BVHs. Replacing a mesh revision rebuilds only that registration's acceleration structure. Chunk identity remains available for filtering; a merged chunk-wide BVH is deferred until profiling justifies it.
4. Streamed terrain is intersected through its authoritative `sampleHeight(x,z)` function, bounded by the owning chunk's X/Z extent. Sampling density comes from source raster dimensions and independent X/Z world spans, not from the dimensions of an individual chunk.
5. The Babylon adapter copies source geometry after authored transforms are baked and before `GeometryRenderer` applies a nonlinear visual projection. Render-only/debug surfaces are excluded unless explicitly marked as optical surfaces.
6. Slice-native rays must start on the target slice and have canonical momentum tangent to its frame. Segment intersections are queried in slice-local coordinates; ray state and hit positions remain ambient R4.
7. Poincare chart and metric validation remains strict. Invalid samples propagate; the tracer does not clip them into valid chart coordinates.
8. Debug ray visualization is a disposable presentation layer. It projects the authoritative trace only when drawing and does not modify the optical path or ray state.
9. Phase 16B does not traverse anomaly topology edges, apply material reflection/refraction/attenuation, or alter production lighting.

## Consequences

- Euclidean and Poincare slices share one geometry registration and tracing API.
- Terrain LOD changes do not change the authoritative terrain surface used for optical hits.
- Chunk streaming lifecycle controls which terrain heightfields are registered.
- The CPU ray solver can now terminate at actual scene geometry and return stable hit data.
- Debug rays can be inspected without making Babylon render coordinates authoritative.
- Cross-slice transfer and aperture momentum laws remain isolated for Phase 16C.

docs/decisions/ADR-0013-four-dimensional-anomaly-optical-bridges.md
_______
# ADR-0013: Cross-Slice Optical Transport Through 4D Anomaly Bridges

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** November 8, 2026
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 16C

## Context

Somnium models 3D worlds as distinct `WorldSlice` objects embedded in ambient R4. Player traversal and continuous W movement already use explicit anomaly topology. Optical propagation now needs to cross between slices without using player traversal permissions or treating an anomaly as a visual portal teleport.

## Decisions

1. **Optical permissions are independent.** An anomaly opts into ray transport with `optics.enabled`, and its optical directionality is controlled by `optics.bidirectional`. Player `traversable` and player `bidirectional` fields do not authorize light.
2. **Rays retain ambient R4 state inside a bridge.** A successful aperture entry changes the metric/context, not the meaning of the ray's four coordinates. Exit occurs only at an explicitly registered destination aperture reachable through the optical graph.
3. **Optical reach is anomaly-specific.** `maxWOpticalReach`, `wCouplingScale`, aperture radius, refractive index, attenuation, transmission, and entry bias are configured independently per anomaly. The radial smootherstep envelope reuses the anomaly center and radii but does not read player modifiers.
4. **Endpoint metrics form the default bridge tangent metric.** The source and destination intrinsic slice metrics are sampled at their respective aperture coordinates, rebased into a common tangent basis, and blended with smootherstep along the bridge normal. Pointwise chart sampling is opt-in because distant points may be outside one endpoint chart's domain.
5. **The initial aperture rule preserves tangential canonical momentum and Hamiltonian.** The normal coefficient is solved from the Hamiltonian constraint. 3D-to-4D entry uses a deterministic aperture-normal/slice-normal launch direction biased toward the anomaly center. This is an idealized transfer law; it does not yet create reflected/refracted branches.
6. **Finite chart boundaries are explicit.** A declared metric-domain guard causes adaptive step reduction and a controlled `chart-domain-boundary` terminal event. Unexpected errors are not swallowed.
7. **The CPU tracer remains authoritative.** Babylon is only used to display slice segments and registered scene geometry. Lighting integration and the eventual optimized backend remain later phases.

## Consequences

- A light ray may traverse a non-player-traversable anomaly, or be blocked by an optically disabled anomaly that players can use.
- One ray can follow an explicitly linked anomaly chain, with transition limits preventing runaway cycles.
- Every slice handoff includes diagnostics for Hamiltonian drift and aperture-tangent momentum preservation.
- The implementation can serve as the reference path for later sunlight, cross-slice shadows, and rendering work.
- Arbitrary 4D obstacles, material reflection/refraction, visible 4D ray-path display, and production lighting are not part of this ADR's implementation scope.

docs/decisions/ADR-0014-view-dependent-anomaly-apertures.md
_______
# ADR-0014: View-Dependent Rendering Through Anomaly Apertures

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** November 8, 2026
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 16D

## Context

The previous anomaly preview used a render-target camera with a fixed pose. The camera could render a connected slice, but its view did not follow the observer's changing position and orientation. The result looked like a static image placed inside an anomaly rim, not a window through which the observer was looking.

The anomaly model also supports more than one geometry type. The view renderer must therefore avoid assuming that every anomaly is a Euclidean 4D sphere.

## Decisions

1. **View permission is independent.** Anomaly viewing has its own `view` configuration. It is not inferred from player `traversable`, visibility, or optical-ray permissions.
2. **Endpoint-frame is the initial dynamic mapping.** The viewer eye offset and tangent camera basis are converted to the local coordinates of the active slice, transferred to the matching endpoint basis, and projected with the remote slice's own transform. This mapping is bidirectional.
3. **Static view remains a valid option.** `view.mapping: 'static'` intentionally retains the authored remote camera pose; it is not used for the live demo aperture.
4. **Aperture shape is declared.** Circle, ellipse, and rectangle render surfaces are supported. The render-target texture is presented on that surface rather than displayed as a standalone rectangular preview card.
5. **Cross-section mathematics is opt-in.** `constant` remains the general fallback. `euclidean-4d-ball` uses the analytic 3D slice radius `sqrt(R²-d²)`, where the slice-normal offset is measured from the resolved ambient anomaly centre by default; a numeric `centerNormalOffset` explicitly overrides that derived value. Other anomaly geometries must supply their own section model before claiming a different geometric profile.
6. **Remote chunk streaming follows the mapped view.** Destination focus and horizontal look direction are derived from the virtual remote camera so the preview does not remain centred on a fixed anchor while the observer looks elsewhere.
7. **Rendering remains non-authoritative.** The remote camera and render target are a presentation mechanism. They do not change authoritative player coordinates, anomaly topology, or the Phase 16C CPU optical ray state.
8. **No atmospheric lighting change in this phase.** Anomaly-driven sky glow or destination recolouring is deferred as an optional art feature. Direct-light transport and surface interaction are a separate later milestone.

## Consequences

- The preview changes when the viewer translates, orbits, or changes camera orientation.
- The same endpoint correspondence works when viewing from either side of the connection.
- Different slice transforms and render scales are respected during mapping.
- The first demo Euclidean-4D mouth can change its visible section size as the observer moves along the slice normal, measured relative to the resolved anomaly centre.
- The design can later accommodate anomaly-specific camera mappings and cross-section evaluators without changing player traversal or optical transport.

## Known limitations

- The current endpoint-frame rule pairs local tangent coordinates by component; anomalies that need custom frame rotation, reflection, lensing, or another projection require an explicit future strategy.
- The current remote-camera portal is not a full per-pixel 4D ray-cast camera and does not provide arbitrary 4D occlusion clipping.
- A live browser/WebGL visual inspection is still required to validate aperture clipping and final composition.

docs/decisions/ADR-0015-anomaly-fed-virtual-spotlight.md
_______
# ADR-0015: Anomaly-Fed Virtual Spotlight

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** November 9, 2026
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 17A

## Context

Phase 16A–16C established engine-independent CPU optical ray integration and explicit cross-slice anomaly transport. Phase 16D established view-dependent aperture rendering. The next demonstrable lighting step is to use a light source located in the Hypercube slice and show its light emerging into the Main World.

A normal Babylon light placed in the source scene cannot itself express the required 4D transport and must not bypass optical topology permissions.

## Decisions

1. The light source is authoritative engine-independent slice-local data with XYZ position/direction, colour, intensity, range, cone angle, exponent, enabled state, and shadow preference.
2. The first prototype uses one spotlight and a deterministic central ray. Point and area emitters are deferred.
3. The ray is lifted into ambient R4 using the source slice frame and traced by the existing anomaly optical tracer. The demo tracer facade restricts this prototype to the explicit direct Hypercube-to-Main-World anomaly.
4. The tracer gains an opt-in `stopAfterAnomalyExit` option. Default tracer behavior is unchanged; light consumers can request the outgoing aperture state without integrating an unused destination tail.
5. A virtual emitter is derived by converting outgoing canonical momentum to destination slice velocity and extrapolating backward from the aperture. Its render-space pose is computed through the destination `SpatialTransform`.
6. Babylon source and receiver spotlights are layer-restricted. A bounded receiving-side shadow map uses nearby eligible Main World meshes. This is a pragmatic direct-light approximation, not complete 4D surface-to-source visibility tracing.
7. Source-side edit controls are isolated from player/camera input while active. The first prototype supports movement and aiming within the source slice only; W movement is deferred.
8. If shadow-map construction is unavailable, receiving-side direct illumination remains enabled without shadows.

## Consequences

- The prototype proves a visible light-source-to-anomaly-to-destination path using the authoritative Phase 16C transport engine.
- Render coordinates are derived from physical slice coordinates; no physical XYZ values are copied directly into a nonlinear destination render space.
- A single ray represents the spotlight's centre direction. Full beam sampling, multiple paths, point-light cubemap shadows, and physically transported shadow rays remain future work.
- Browser/WebGL testing is still required to verify actual lighting and shadow appearance.

docs/decisions/ADR-0016-spherical-mouth-and-cylinder-aperture-continuity.md
_______
# ADR-0016: Spherical Anomaly Mouth and Tapered-Cylinder Aperture Continuity

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** November 9, 2026
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 17G

## Context

Phase 17E introduced a tapered 4D cylinder whose 3D W-slice is a sphere with an interpolated radius. Phase 17F then added an additional portal-preview aperture scale curve during destination approach. Those two effects both influenced the apparent mouth size and could produce an abrupt/reversing change when traversal progress was cleared or the active slice changed at the destination endpoint.

The demo also used a flat circular render-target surface and retained a decorative torus rim from an older portal-mouth representation. The user requested a three-dimensional spherical opening while retaining the flat preview as an option.

## Decisions

1. **One size authority for tapered cylinders.** When `view.interiorBoundary === 'open-4d-cylinder'`, `calculateAnomalyApertureScale()` returns 1 in both travel directions, during transit, and after handoff. The live `AnomalyBoundaryRenderer` cylinder cross-section is the sole changing diameter signal. The destination approach remains a camera-pose transport effect.
2. **Keep legacy 4D ball sizing for other anomalies.** The analytic `sqrt(R²-d²)` aperture section remains active when the anomaly does not use the tapered-cylinder boundary. This avoids changing unrelated anomaly types.
3. **Preview surface is a separate configurable choice.** `previewSurface: 'flat'` preserves the existing flat surface and remains the default. `previewSurface: 'spherical'` deforms a Disc into a concave spherical cap for circle/ellipse apertures. Rectangular spherical previews are rejected rather than approximated silently.
4. **Preserve image projection.** The spherical-cap deformation changes vertex positions and recomputes normals/bounds while retaining the render-target UV coordinates. The destination view remains an image from the transported remote camera; it is not a full per-pixel 4D ray-cast view.
5. **Legacy rim is opt-in.** `showRim` defaults to false. The old portal torus is created only for anomalies explicitly requesting `showRim: true`. Generic torus props elsewhere in the demo are unrelated.
6. **No physical geometry changes.** Canonical anomaly endpoints, region bounds, traversal, optical connectivity, and destination-world geometry remain unchanged.

## Consequences

- A tapered-cylinder mouth cannot acquire a second, transit-progress-dependent scale curve that snaps or reverses at the endpoint handoff.
- The 3D cylinder cross-section can expand continuously toward the destination while the transported remote camera separately approaches its endpoint.
- The direct Hypercube-to-Main-World demo uses a concave spherical preview mouth; other anomalies can retain the flat surface.
- The decorative torus ring is absent unless explicitly enabled.

## Known limitations

- The spherical preview is a concave cap, not a complete sphere, refractive lens, or physically modelled 3D portal volume.
- Spherical preview geometry supports circular and elliptical apertures only.
- The current tapered cylinder renderer requires a W-aligned axis.
- Nonlinear slice transforms can distort the displayed cap; this follows the slice renderer's existing presentation mapping and requires visual inspection.
- No live browser/WebGL validation was available for this change. Texture appearance, transparency ordering, depth composition, and perceived handoff continuity remain manual validation items.

docs/decisions/ADR-0017-complete-sphere-destination-aperture.md
_______
# ADR-0017: Complete-Sphere Destination Aperture and Inner-Mouth Growth

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** November 9, 2026
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 17H

## Context

Phase 17G's spherical-cap preview looked like a shallow curved disc rather than a complete spherical opening. The destination mouth also needed its own apparent-size progression: it should begin small at the far end of the anomaly tube and grow faster than the tube's outer cross-section as the observer traverses the corridor.

## Decisions

1. Spherical destination previews use a complete Babylon sphere mesh, not a deformed disc or spherical cap.
2. The live destination render-target remains front-orthographically projected onto the visible sphere surface. This preserves a camera-like image instead of interpreting the render target as an equirectangular environment map.
3. Flat circular/elliptical previews remain available as an explicit compatibility option.
4. The tapered 4D cylinder remains the authoritative outer boundary. The destination sphere has an independent growth curve with default start scale 0.08 and growth exponent 0.55.
5. Growth is calculated from traversal progress normalized from the viewer's entry mouth. Source and destination radii are swapped in reverse traversal; no W-sign heuristic controls apparent scale.
6. The sphere's physical radius is clamped to the current outer tube radius and meets that radius at the far endpoint. The returned Babylon mesh scale is relative to the entry mouth's authored radius and can be greater or less than one.
7. The legacy spherical-cap geometry helper remains exported for compatibility but is not used by the new spherical preview path.
8. This decision does not change physical anomaly geometry, endpoint coordinates, traversal permissions, or W-slice movement.

## Consequences

- The destination mouth has full three-dimensional depth and can be seen from either side.
- Its apparent/angular size can grow faster than the outer tube as the observer approaches the far mouth.
- The sphere's front-orthographic texture projection may distort at extreme off-axis viewpoints; live browser inspection will determine whether a later perspective-aware projection is warranted.
- The separate Main World endpoint / W-slice alignment issue remains outside this phase.

docs/decisions/ADR-0018-bidirectional-spherical-anomaly-passage.md
_______
# ADR-0018: Bidirectional Spherical Anomaly Passage Presentation

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Phase:** Geometry Phase 17I
- **Date:** November 9, 2026

## Context

Phase 17H represented only the remote destination mouth. The desired 4D traversal metaphor has two endpoints visible from within a dark transitional region: the source entrance behind the player and the destination exit ahead. The two endpoints are physically separated along W, which cannot be directly displayed as a fourth spatial axis in the 3D camera.

## Decision

Represent the two endpoints as independent complete spherical renderers separated in a configurable 3D presentation frame. In follow mode, derive the default display axis from the player's travel heading; in free-camera mode, capture the travel-aligned camera forward direction at anomaly entry. Allow an explicit axis override. Keep the entrance one camera inset behind the initial display camera and the exit ahead. Advance the display camera along the axis as normalized W traversal progress changes. Perspective produces the opposing apparent angular-size progression without introducing a second competing sphere-growth animation. The captured axis remains stable when the player later orbits the camera.

Render the source world into the entrance sphere and the destination world into the exit sphere. Isolate both surfaces on a dedicated render layer and use a black scene clear color while the passage is active. Do not billboard the surfaces or change canonical 4D coordinates, collision, topology, or world/chunk ownership.

## Consequences

- Camera orbit remains available for inspecting both mouths from different directions.
- Actual perspective contributes to the apparent entrance shrinkage and exit growth.
- Reverse traversal swaps endpoint identities and radii based on active traversal orientation.
- Two additional render targets are created per eligible anomaly presentation.
- Live visual validation is still required for texture projection, composition, performance, and endpoint handoff.

Commented out index.html, for display within an HTML page.

src/atmosphere/air-pressure-field.js
_______

class AirPressureField {
    constructor(options = {}) {
        this.time = 0;

        this.spatialScale = options.spatialScale ?? 100000;

        this.gradientStep = options.gradientStep ?? 5000;

        this.windStrength = options.windStrength ?? 0.85;

        this.maxWindSpeed = options.maxWindSpeed ?? 1.1;

        this.prevailingWind = new BABYLON.Vector3(
            0.28,
            0,
            0.12
        );

        this.wind = new BABYLON.Vector3();
    }

    update(deltaTime) {
        this.time += Math.max(0, deltaTime);
    }

    pressureAt(x, z, time = this.time) {
        const scale = this.spatialScale;

        const px = x / scale;
        const pz = z / scale;

        const wave1 = Math.sin(
            px * 0.85 +
            pz * 0.38 +
            time * 0.018
        );

        const wave2 = Math.cos(
            pz * 0.72 -
            px * 0.31 -
            time * 0.012
        );

        const wave3 = Math.sin(
            (px + pz) * 0.42 +
            time * 0.009
        );

        return (
            wave1 * 0.42 +
            wave2 * 0.34 +
            wave3 * 0.24
        );
    }

    sample(position, time = this.time) {
        const x = position.x;
        const z = position.z;
        const h = this.gradientStep;

        const pressure = this.pressureAt(
            x,
            z,
            time
        );

        // Estimate the horizontal pressure gradient.
        const gradientX = (
            this.pressureAt(x + h, z, time) -
            this.pressureAt(x - h, z, time)
        ) / (2 * h);

        const gradientZ = (
            this.pressureAt(x, z + h, time) -
            this.pressureAt(x, z - h, time)
        ) / (2 * h);

        // Air flows approximately from higher pressure
        // toward lower pressure.
        let windX =
            -gradientX *
            this.spatialScale *
            this.windStrength;

        let windZ =
            -gradientZ *
            this.spatialScale *
            this.windStrength;

        windX += this.prevailingWind.x;
        windZ += this.prevailingWind.z;

        const magnitude = Math.hypot(
            windX,
            windZ
        );

        if (magnitude > this.maxWindSpeed) {
            const factor =
                this.maxWindSpeed / magnitude;

            windX *= factor;
            windZ *= factor;
        }

        this.wind.set(
            windX,
            0,
            windZ
        );

        return {
            pressure,
            wind: this.wind.clone()
        };
    }

    getStats(position) {
        const sample = this.sample(position);

        return {
            pressure: sample.pressure,
            windSpeed: sample.wind.length(),
            windDirection: sample.wind.clone().normalize()
        };
    }
}

export { AirPressureField };


src/atmosphere/cloud-generator.js

class CloudGenerator {
    constructor(config) {
        this.config = config;
    }

    createRandom(seed = 91827) {
        let state = seed >>> 0;

        return () => {
            state = (
                Math.imul(state, 1664525) +
                1013904223
            ) >>> 0;

            return state / 4294967296;
        };
    }

    generate(
        position,
        scale,
        maxDepth = 2,
        seed = 91827
    ) {
        const matrices = [];
        const random = this.createRandom(seed);

        this.generateRecursive(
            position.clone(),
            scale,
            maxDepth,
            0,
            random,
            matrices
        );

        return matrices;
    }

    generateRecursive(
        position,
        scale,
        maxDepth,
        currentDepth,
        random,
        matrices
    ) {
        const config = this.config;
        const irregularity = config.irregularity;

        const dimensions = new BABYLON.Vector3(
            scale * config.width *
                (0.80 + random() * irregularity),
            scale * config.height *
                (0.80 + random() * irregularity),
            scale * config.depth *
                (0.80 + random() * irregularity)
        );

        const rotation =
            BABYLON.Quaternion.RotationYawPitchRoll(
                random() * 0.35,
                (random() - 0.5) * 0.22,
                (random() - 0.5) * 0.22
            );

        matrices.push(
            BABYLON.Matrix.Compose(
                dimensions,
                rotation,
                position
            )
        );

        if (currentDepth >= maxDepth) {
            return;
        }

        for (
            let i = 0;
            i < config.branchCount;
            i++
        ) {
            const angle = random() * Math.PI * 2;

            const horizontal =
                scale *
                config.horizontalSpread *
                (0.45 + random() * 0.75);

            const vertical =
                scale * config.verticalSpread;

            let verticalOffset =
                (random() * 2 - 1) * vertical;

            if (config.height > 2) {
                verticalOffset =
                    verticalOffset * 0.45 +
                    Math.abs(verticalOffset) * 0.75;
            }

            const offset = new BABYLON.Vector3(
                Math.cos(angle) * horizontal,
                verticalOffset,
                Math.sin(angle) * horizontal
            );

            const childPosition =
                position.add(offset);

            const childScale =
                scale *
                config.scaleDecay *
                (0.78 + random() * 0.38);

            this.generateRecursive(
                childPosition,
                childScale,
                maxDepth,
                currentDepth + 1,
                random,
                matrices
            );
        }
    }
}

export { CloudGenerator };

src/atmosphere/cloud-system.js
_______

import { Cloud } from "./cloud.js";

import { CloudSpecies } from "./cloud-species.js";

import { CloudGenerator } from "./cloud-generator.js";

import { AirPressureField } from "./air-pressure-field.js";

import { CloudRenderer } from "../rendering/cloud-renderer.js";


class CloudSystem {
    constructor(
        scene,
        terrain,
        waterSystem,
        hydrology,
        rainSystem
    ) {
        this.scene = scene;

        this.terrain = terrain;
        this.waterSystem = waterSystem;
        this.hydrology = hydrology;
        this.rainSystem = rainSystem;

        this.clouds = [];

        this.renderer = new CloudRenderer(scene);

        this.maxClouds = 100;

        this.rainingCloud = null;

        // Atmospheric circulation.
        this.pressureField = new AirPressureField();

        this.elapsed = 0;

        // Regional weather classification.
        this.weatherCellSize = 100000;

        this.weatherCells = new Map();

        // Rendering update frequency.
        this.renderAccumulator = 0;
        this.renderInterval = 0.4;

        this.renderDirty = false;

        this.disposed = false;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // REGIONAL WEATHER
    // ------------------------------------------

    getWeatherCellKey(x, z) {
        const cx = Math.floor(
            x / this.weatherCellSize
        );

        const cz = Math.floor(
            z / this.weatherCellSize
        );

        return `${cx},${cz}`;
    }

    getWeatherRegime(position) {
        const key = this.getWeatherCellKey(
            position.x,
            position.z
        );

        if (this.weatherCells.has(key)) {
            return this.weatherCells.get(key);
        }

        const centerX =
            (Math.floor(
                position.x / this.weatherCellSize
            ) + 0.5) * this.weatherCellSize;

        const centerZ =
            (Math.floor(
                position.z / this.weatherCellSize
            ) + 0.5) * this.weatherCellSize;

        const center = new BABYLON.Vector3(
            centerX,
            position.y,
            centerZ
        );

        const atmospheric =
            this.pressureField.sample(center);

        const moisture = BABYLON.Scalar.Clamp(
            this.waterSystem.getEvaporationPotential(
                center
            ),
            0,
            1
        );

        // Lower pressure favors rising air.
        // Moisture is required for deep convection.
        const instability = BABYLON.Scalar.Clamp(
            0.5 - atmospheric.pressure,
            0,
            1
        );

        let regime = "stable";

        if (
            moisture >= 0.58 &&
            atmospheric.pressure <= -0.12 &&
            instability >= 0.62
        ) {
            regime = "storm";
        } else if (
            moisture >= 0.36 &&
            atmospheric.pressure <= 0.20
        ) {
            regime = "convective";
        }

        this.weatherCells.set(key, regime);

        return regime;
    }

    selectSpecies(regime, random = Math.random) {
        const value = random();

        switch (regime) {
            case "storm":
                if (value < 0.20) {
                    return "cumulus";
                }

                if (value < 0.80) {
                    return "towering";
                }

                return "cumulonimbus";

            case "convective":
                return value < 0.45
                    ? "cumulus"
                    : "towering";

            default:
                return value < 0.85
                    ? "cumulus"
                    : "towering";
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // CLOUD GENERATION
    // ------------------------------------------

    generate(count = 35) {
        if (this.disposed) return;

        this.clouds = [];

        this.weatherCells.clear();

        this.renderer.clear();

        const actualCount = Math.min(
            count,
            this.maxClouds
        );

        for (
            let i = 0;
            i < actualCount;
            i++
        ) {
            const terrainPosition =
                this.terrain.sample();

            if (!terrainPosition) continue;

            const weatherRegime =
                this.getWeatherRegime(
                    terrainPosition
                );

            const speciesName =
                this.selectSpecies(weatherRegime);

            const config =
                CloudSpecies[speciesName];

            const scale =
                config.scale *
                (
                    speciesName === "cumulonimbus"
                        ? 0.78 + Math.random() * 0.35
                        : 0.70 + Math.random() * 0.55
                );

            const position =
                terrainPosition.add(
                    new BABYLON.Vector3(
                        0,
                        90 + Math.random() * 65,
                        0
                    )
                );

            const cloud = new Cloud(
                position,
                speciesName,
                scale,
                config,
                weatherRegime
            );

            // Generate the formation relative to
            // its own origin, not world coordinates.
            const generator = new CloudGenerator(
                config
            );

            cloud.geometryMatrices =
                generator.generate(
                    BABYLON.Vector3.Zero(),
                    scale,
                    config.recursionDepth,
                    i + 91827
                );

            // Start with the prevailing wind.
            const atmospheric =
                this.pressureField.sample(position);

            cloud.velocity.copyFrom(
                atmospheric.wind.scale(0.35)
            );

            this.clouds.push(cloud);
        }

        this.updateRendering(true);
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // WIND AND CLOUD MOVEMENT
    // ------------------------------------------

    updateWind(cloud, deltaTime) {
        const atmospheric =
            this.pressureField.sample(
                cloud.position
            );

        const target = atmospheric.wind;

        // Gradually approach the local wind velocity.
        // This avoids abrupt changes between regions.
        const response = 1 - Math.exp(
            -cloud.windResponse * deltaTime
        );

        cloud.velocity.x +=
            (target.x - cloud.velocity.x) *
            response;

        cloud.velocity.z +=
            (target.z - cloud.velocity.z) *
            response;

        // Small, smooth atmospheric turbulence.
        const turbulence =
            cloud.windTurbulence;

        const phase = this.elapsed * 0.12;

        cloud.velocity.x +=
            Math.sin(phase + cloud.position.z * 0.0001) *
            turbulence *
            deltaTime;

        cloud.velocity.z +=
            Math.cos(phase + cloud.position.x * 0.0001) *
            turbulence *
            deltaTime;

        cloud.position.x +=
            cloud.velocity.x * deltaTime * 0.5;

        cloud.position.z +=
            cloud.velocity.z * deltaTime * 0.5;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // CLOUD SIMULATION
    // ------------------------------------------

    update(deltaYears) {
        if (this.disposed) return;

        const deltaTime = Math.max(
            0,
            Math.min(deltaYears, 0.25)
        );

        this.elapsed += deltaTime;

        this.pressureField.update(deltaTime);

        let activeRainCloud = null;

        for (const cloud of this.clouds) {
            this.updateCloud(cloud, deltaTime);

            if (
                cloud.isRaining &&
                (
                    !activeRainCloud ||
                    cloud.rainIntensity >
                    activeRainCloud.rainIntensity
                )
            ) {
                activeRainCloud = cloud;
            }
        }

        this.rainingCloud = activeRainCloud;

        if (activeRainCloud) {
            const rainPosition =
                activeRainCloud.position.clone();

            rainPosition.y -= 10;

            this.rainSystem.start(
                rainPosition,
                activeRainCloud.rainIntensity
            );
        } else {
            this.rainSystem.stop();
        }

        this.renderAccumulator += deltaTime;

        if (
            this.renderDirty &&
            this.renderAccumulator >=
                this.renderInterval
        ) {
            this.updateRendering();

            this.renderAccumulator = 0;
        }
    }

    updateCloud(cloud, deltaTime) {
        this.updateWind(cloud, deltaTime);

        // Cache environmental sampling.
        cloud.environmentSampleTimer -= deltaTime;

        if (cloud.environmentSampleTimer <= 0) {
            cloud.evaporationPotential =
                BABYLON.Scalar.Clamp(
                    this.waterSystem.getEvaporationPotential(
                        cloud.position
                    ),
                    0,
                    1
                );

            cloud.environmentSampleTimer = 1.0;
        }

        // Moisture accumulation.
        if (!cloud.isRaining) {
            cloud.waterContent +=
                cloud.absorptionRate *
                cloud.evaporationPotential *
                deltaTime;
        }

        cloud.waterContent = Math.min(
            cloud.waterContent,
            cloud.maxWaterCapacity
        );

        // Precipitation threshold.
        if (
            cloud.waterContent >=
            cloud.maxWaterCapacity
        ) {
            this.startRain(cloud);
        }

        // Rainfall duration.
        if (cloud.isRaining) {
            cloud.rainRemaining -= deltaTime;

            if (cloud.rainRemaining <= 0) {
                cloud.isRaining = false;
                cloud.rainIntensity = 0;
                cloud.rainRemaining = 0;
            }
        }

        this.renderDirty = true;
    }

    startRain(cloud) {
        cloud.isRaining = true;

        cloud.rainRemaining =
            cloud.rainDuration;

        cloud.rainIntensity =
            0.5 + cloud.moistureRatio * 1.5;

        const releasedWater =
            cloud.maxWaterCapacity * 0.45;

        cloud.waterContent -= releasedWater;

        const rainfallAmount =
            0.25 * cloud.rainIntensity;

        const rainfallRadius =
            cloud.scale * 4;

        this.hydrology.addRain(
            cloud.position,
            rainfallRadius,
            rainfallAmount
        );
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // RENDERING
    // ------------------------------------------

    updateRendering(force = false) {
        if (
            !force &&
            !this.renderDirty
        ) {
            return;
        }

        this.renderer.clear();

        for (const cloud of this.clouds) {
            const localMatrices =
                cloud.geometryMatrices;

            if (!localMatrices) continue;

            const worldMatrices = [];

            for (const localMatrix of localMatrices) {
                const matrix = localMatrix.clone();

                // Translate the local formation into
                // its current world position.
                matrix.m[12] += cloud.position.x;
                matrix.m[13] += cloud.position.y;
                matrix.m[14] += cloud.position.z;

                worldMatrices.push(matrix);
            }

            this.renderer.addCloud(
                worldMatrices,
                cloud.moistureRatio,
                cloud.speciesName,
                cloud.position
            );
        }

        this.renderer.update();

        this.renderDirty = false;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------
    // DIAGNOSTICS
    // ------------------------------------------

    getStats() {
        const speciesCounts = {
            cumulus: 0,
            towering: 0,
            cumulonimbus: 0
        };

        for (const cloud of this.clouds) {
            speciesCounts[cloud.speciesName]++;
        }

        return {
            totalClouds: this.clouds.length,
            speciesCounts,
            weatherRegions: this.weatherCells.size,
            rainingClouds: this.clouds.filter(
                cloud => cloud.isRaining
            ).length,
            averageWindSpeed:
                this.clouds.length
                    ? this.clouds.reduce(
                        (sum, cloud) =>
                            sum + cloud.velocity.length(),
                        0
                    ) / this.clouds.length
                    : 0
        };
    }

    dispose() {
        if (this.disposed) return;

        this.disposed = true;

        this.rainSystem.stop();

        this.renderer.mesh.dispose();

        this.clouds.length = 0;

        this.weatherCells.clear();
    }
}

export { CloudSystem };


src/atmosphere/cloud.js
_______

export class Cloud {
    constructor(position, speciesName, scale, config) {
        this.position = position.clone();
        this.speciesName = speciesName;
        this.scale = scale;
        this.baseScale = scale;
        this.config = config;

        this.waterContent = 0;
        this.maxWaterCapacity = config.moistureCapacity ?? 100;
        this.absorptionRate = config.absorptionRate ?? 16;

        this.rainIntensity = 0;
        this.rainRemaining = 0;
        this.rainDuration = config.rainDuration ?? 1.5;
        this.isRaining = false;

        // Atmospheric wind state.
        this.velocity = BABYLON.Vector3.Zero();
        this.windTarget = BABYLON.Vector3.Zero();
        this.windResponse = 0.12;

        this.localMoisture = 0;
        this.evaporationPotential = 0;
        this.environmentSampleTimer = 0;

        // Persistent geometry cache.
        this.moistureAtLastRender = -1;
        this.baseGeometryMatrices = null;
        this.baseGeometryPosition = null;

        this.geometrySeed = 1;
    }

    get moistureRatio() {
        return BABYLON.Scalar.Clamp(
            this.waterContent / this.maxWaterCapacity,
            0,
            1
        );
    }

    get isStormCloud() {
        return this.speciesName === "cumulonimbus";
    }

    updateWind(target, deltaSeconds) {
        this.windTarget.copyFrom(target);

        const response = 1 - Math.exp(
            -this.windResponse * deltaSeconds
        );

        BABYLON.Vector3.LerpToRef(
            this.velocity,
            this.windTarget,
            response,
            this.velocity
        );

        this.position.addInPlace(
            this.velocity.scale(deltaSeconds*0.01)
        );
    }
}


src/buildings/building-generator.js

class BuildingGenerator {
    constructor(options = {}) {
        this.defaultWallHeight = options.wallHeight ?? 3.2;
        this.defaultWallThickness = options.wallThickness ?? 0.18;
    }

    createBox(output, kind, position, dimensions, rotation = 0, material = "wall") {
        if (
            dimensions.x <= 0 ||
            dimensions.y <= 0 ||
            dimensions.z <= 0
        ) return;

        output.push({
            kind,
            position,
            dimensions,
            rotation,
            material
        });
    }

    getRoomEdges(room) {
        const b = room.bounds;

        return [
            {
                side: "north",
                x1: b.minX, z1: b.minZ,
                x2: b.maxX, z2: b.minZ
            },
            {
                side: "south",
                x1: b.minX, z1: b.maxZ,
                x2: b.maxX, z2: b.maxZ
            },
            {
                side: "west",
                x1: b.minX, z1: b.minZ,
                x2: b.minX, z2: b.maxZ
            },
            {
                side: "east",
                x1: b.maxX, z1: b.minZ,
                x2: b.maxX, z2: b.maxZ
            }
        ];
    }

    edgeKey(edge, floor) {
        const a = `${edge.x1},${edge.z1}`;
        const b = `${edge.x2},${edge.z2}`;

        return [
            floor,
            ...[a, b].sort()
        ].join(":");
    }

    generateWall(output, edge, openings, floorY, height, thickness) {
        const horizontal = edge.side === "north" ||
            edge.side === "south";

        const length = horizontal
            ? Math.abs(edge.x2 - edge.x1)
            : Math.abs(edge.z2 - edge.z1);

        const centerX = (edge.x1 + edge.x2) * 0.5;
        const centerZ = (edge.z1 + edge.z2) * 0.5;

        const wallRotation = horizontal ? 0 : Math.PI / 2;

        const centerY = floorY + height * 0.5;

        const validOpenings = openings
            .filter(o => o.side === edge.side)
            .map(o => ({
                ...o,
                center: o.offset * length
            }))
            .filter(o =>
                o.center - o.width * 0.5 >= 0 &&
                o.center + o.width * 0.5 <= length
            )
            .sort((a, b) => a.center - b.center);

        let cursor = 0;

        const addSegment = (start, end) => {
            if (end - start <= 0.01) return;

            const middle = (start + end) * 0.5;
            const along = middle - length * 0.5;

            this.createBox(
                output,
                "walls",
                {
                    x: centerX + (horizontal ? along : 0),
                    y: centerY,
                    z: centerZ + (horizontal ? 0 : along)
                },
                {
                    x: horizontal ? end - start : thickness,
                    y: height,
                    z: horizontal ? thickness : end - start
                },
                0,
                "wall"
            );
        };

        for (const opening of validOpenings) {
            const start = opening.center - opening.width * 0.5;
            const end = opening.center + opening.width * 0.5;

            // Full-height wall before the opening.
            addSegment(cursor, start);

            const along = opening.center - length * 0.5;
            const x = centerX + (horizontal ? along : 0);
            const z = centerZ + (horizontal ? 0 : along);

            // Windows retain their sill and lintel.
            if (opening.type === "window") {
                if (opening.sill > 0) {
                    this.createBox(
                        output,
                        "walls",
                        { x, y: floorY + opening.sill * 0.5, z },
                        {
                            x: horizontal ? opening.width : thickness,
                            y: opening.sill,
                            z: horizontal ? thickness : opening.width
                        }
                    );
                }

                const top = opening.sill + opening.height;
                const remaining = height - top;

                if (remaining > 0) {
                    this.createBox(
                        output,
                        "walls",
                        {
                            x,
                            y: floorY + top + remaining * 0.5,
                            z
                        },
                        {
                            x: horizontal ? opening.width : thickness,
                            y: remaining,
                            z: horizontal ? thickness : opening.width
                        }
                    );
                }

                this.createBox(
                    output,
                    "glazing",
                    {
                        x,
                        y: floorY + opening.sill + opening.height * 0.5,
                        z
                    },
                    {
                        x: horizontal ? opening.width * 0.88 : 0.035,
                        y: opening.height * 0.88,
                        z: horizontal ? 0.035 : opening.width * 0.88
                    },
                    0,
                    "glass"
                );
            } else {
                // Door frame components.
                const frame = 0.075;

                for (const side of [-1, 1]) {
                    this.createBox(
                        output,
                        "trim",
                        {
                            x: x + (horizontal ? side * (opening.width * 0.5 - frame * 0.5) : 0),
                            y: floorY + opening.height * 0.5,
                            z: z + (horizontal ? 0 : side * (opening.width * 0.5 - frame * 0.5))
                        },
                        {
                            x: horizontal ? frame : thickness * 0.75,
                            y: opening.height,
                            z: horizontal ? thickness * 0.75 : frame
                        },
                        0,
                        "wood"
                    );
                }

                this.createBox(
                    output,
                    "trim",
                    { x, y: floorY + opening.height, z },
                    {
                        x: horizontal ? opening.width : thickness * 0.75,
                        y: frame,
                        z: horizontal ? thickness * 0.75 : opening.width
                    },
                    0,
                    "wood"
                );

                // Door leaf is a separate component.
                this.createBox(
                    output,
                    "doors",
                    {
                        x,
                        y: floorY + opening.height * 0.5,
                        z
                    },
                    {
                        x: horizontal ? opening.width * 0.94 : 0.07,
                        y: opening.height * 0.94,
                        z: horizontal ? 0.07 : opening.width * 0.94
                    },
                    0,
                    "wood"
                );
            }

            cursor = end;
        }

        addSegment(cursor, length);
    }

    generate(building) {
        building.validate();

        const output = [];

        const edges = new Map();

        for (const room of building.rooms) {
            const floorY = room.floor * room.wallHeight;
            const b = room.bounds;

            this.createBox(
                output,
                "floors",
                {
                    x: (b.minX + b.maxX) * 0.5,
                    y: floorY - room.floorThickness * 0.5,
                    z: (b.minZ + b.maxZ) * 0.5
                },
                {
                    x: b.maxX - b.minX,
                    y: room.floorThickness,
                    z: b.maxZ - b.minZ
                },
                0,
                "floor"
            );

            this.createBox(
                output,
                "ceilings",
                {
                    x: (b.minX + b.maxX) * 0.5,
                    y: floorY + room.wallHeight,
                    z: (b.minZ + b.maxZ) * 0.5
                },
                {
                    x: b.maxX - b.minX,
                    y: 0.12,
                    z: b.maxZ - b.minZ
                },
                0,
                "ceiling"
            );

            for (const edge of this.getRoomEdges(room)) {
                const key = this.edgeKey(edge, room.floor);

                if (!edges.has(key)) {
                    edges.set(key, {
                        edge,
                        openings: [],
                        floorY,
                        height: room.wallHeight,
                        thickness: room.wallThickness
                    });
                }

		edges.get(key).openings.push(
    ...(room.openings ?? [])
        .filter(o => o.side === edge.side)
        .map(o => ({
            ...o,
            side: edges.get(key).edge.side
        }))
);

            }
        }

        for (const item of edges.values()) {
            this.generateWall(
                output,
                item.edge,
                item.openings,
                item.floorY,
                item.height,
                item.thickness
            );
        }

        // Explicitly placed modular objects.
        const components = [
            ...building.components,
            ...building.furniture,
            ...building.fixtures
        ];

        for (const component of components) {
            const kind = component.kind === "furniture"
                ? "furniture"
                : component.kind === "fixture"
                    ? "fixtures"
                    : component.kind;

            this.createBox(
                output,
                kind,
                component.position,
                component.dimensions,
                component.rotation,
                component.material
            );
        }

        return output;
    }
}

export { BuildingGenerator };


src/buildings/building-model.js

function createId(prefix = "building") {
    return `${prefix}-${globalThis.crypto?.randomUUID?.() ??
        `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`}`;
}

function clone(value) {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value));
}

class BuildingModel {
    constructor(options = {}) {
        this.id = options.id ?? createId();

        this.name = options.name ?? "New Building";
        this.type = options.type ?? "residential";

        this.position = {
            x: options.position?.x ?? 0,
            y: options.position?.y ?? 0,
            z: options.position?.z ?? 0
        };

        this.rotation = options.rotation ?? 0;

        this.rooms = clone(options.rooms ?? []);
        this.furniture = clone(options.furniture ?? []);
        this.fixtures = clone(options.fixtures ?? []);

        // Independently placed architectural elements.
        this.components = clone(options.components ?? []);

        this.metadata = {
            version: 1,
            createdAt: options.metadata?.createdAt ??
                new Date().toISOString()
        };
    }

    addRoom(options = {}) {
        const room = {
            id: createId("room"),
            name: options.name ?? "Room",
            floor: options.floor ?? 0,

            bounds: {
                minX: options.minX ?? 0,
                maxX: options.maxX ?? 8,
                minZ: options.minZ ?? 0,
                maxZ: options.maxZ ?? 8
            },

            wallHeight: options.wallHeight ?? 3.2,
            wallThickness: options.wallThickness ?? 0.18,

            floorThickness: options.floorThickness ?? 0.15,

            openings: clone(options.openings ?? [])
        };

        this.rooms.push(room);
        return room;
    }

    addOpening(roomId, options = {}) {
        const room = this.rooms.find(r => r.id === roomId);

        if (!room) {
            throw new Error("Room not found.");
        }

        const opening = {
            id: createId("opening"),
            type: options.type ?? "door",
            side: options.side ?? "north",
            offset: options.offset ?? 0.5,
            width: options.width ?? 0.9,
            height: options.height ?? 2.1,
            sill: options.sill ?? 0
        };

        room.openings.push(opening);
        return opening;
    }

    addComponent(options = {}) {
        const component = {
            id: createId("component"),
            kind: options.kind ?? "furniture",
            type: options.type ?? "custom",

            position: {
                x: options.position?.x ?? 0,
                y: options.position?.y ?? 0,
                z: options.position?.z ?? 0
            },

            dimensions: {
                x: options.dimensions?.x ?? 1,
                y: options.dimensions?.y ?? 1,
                z: options.dimensions?.z ?? 1
            },

            rotation: options.rotation ?? 0,
            material: options.material ?? "wood"
        };

        this.components.push(component);
        return component;
    }

    addFurniture(options = {}) {
        return this.addComponent({
            ...options,
            kind: "furniture"
        });
    }

    validate() {
        if (!this.id || !Array.isArray(this.rooms)) {
            throw new Error("Invalid building.");
        }

        for (const room of this.rooms) {
            const b = room.bounds;

            if (
                !b ||
                ![b.minX, b.maxX, b.minZ, b.maxZ].every(Number.isFinite) ||
                b.maxX <= b.minX ||
                b.maxZ <= b.minZ ||
                !Number.isFinite(room.floor) ||
                !Number.isFinite(room.wallHeight) ||
                room.wallHeight <= 0
            ) {
                throw new Error(`Invalid room: ${room.id}`);
            }

            for (const opening of room.openings ?? []) {
                if (
                    !["north", "south", "east", "west"].includes(opening.side) ||
                    !["door", "window"].includes(opening.type) ||
                    !Number.isFinite(opening.offset) ||
                    opening.offset < 0 ||
                    opening.offset > 1 ||
                    !Number.isFinite(opening.width) ||
                    opening.width <= 0 ||
                    !Number.isFinite(opening.height) ||
                    opening.height <= 0 ||
                    !Number.isFinite(opening.sill) ||
                    opening.sill < 0 ||
                    opening.sill + opening.height > room.wallHeight
                ) {
                    throw new Error(`Invalid opening in room ${room.id}`);
                }
            }
        }

        return true;
    }

    serialize() {
        this.validate();

        return {
            id: this.id,
            type: "building",
            version: 1,
            name: this.name,
            buildingType: this.type,
            position: clone(this.position),
            rotation: this.rotation,
            rooms: clone(this.rooms),
            furniture: clone(this.furniture),
            fixtures: clone(this.fixtures),
            components: clone(this.components),
            metadata: clone(this.metadata)
        };
    }

    static deserialize(data) {
        if (!data || data.type !== "building" ||
            ![1].includes(data.version)) {
            throw new Error("Unsupported building record.");
        }

        const building = new BuildingModel({
            id: data.id,
            name: data.name,
            type: data.buildingType,
            position: data.position,
            rotation: data.rotation,
            rooms: data.rooms,
            furniture: data.furniture,
            fixtures: data.fixtures,
            components: data.components,
            metadata: data.metadata
        });

        building.validate();
        return building;
    }
}

export { BuildingModel, createId };


src/buildings/building-renderer.js
